requirements.text: The Correlator Backend System must receive data from the Correlator in real-time.
The Correlator Backend System must assemble time-series from the Correlator lag output.
The Correlator Backend System must perform Fourier Transforms of the assembled time series.
The Correlator Backend System must perform a limited number of additional processes upon user request.
The Correlator Backend System must deliver suitably formatted results to the End-to-End System.
The BE shall receive LTA or Speed Dump Lag Frames from the Correlator.
The transfer shall take place in such a manner that all data needed to perform any Fourier Transform shows-up on a single processor.
The BE shall receive, via M&C, State Count data produced by the Correlator.
The BE shall receive, via M&C, data and parameters specific to the current EVLA Observational Mode needed for processing the Correlator Lag values.
The BE shall receive, via M&C, all meta-data necessary to format BE results for delivery to the E2E.
The BE shall provide operational status data to and receive control data from the M&C System.
The BE shall provide error and warning reports to M&C as operating conditions warrant.
The BE shall deliver formatted final results to the e2e System.
The BE shall acknowledge receipt of all data received from M&C.
The BE shall notify M&C of any detected interruptions of data delivery from the Correlator.
The BE shall verify successful delivery of output to the e2e.
The BE shall guarantee safe delivery of all internal messages.
The BE shall be able to handle lag frames of less than 128 values.
The BE shall be able to handle lag sets up to a maximum size of 262,144 values.
All users of the system shall login using some form of unique identification.
All login attempts shall be done in a secure manner.
A system administrator shall have unrestricted access to all aspects of the system.
All login attempts shall be encrypted using industry-standard protocols such as TLS 1.2 or higher, and passwords must be stored using salted cryptographic hashes (e.g., Argon2 or bcrypt).
Define the maximum duration and data volume of a Correlator burst that the system must buffer without data loss.
Specify the maximum duration of E2E system downtime the Backend must be able to buffer before data loss occurs.
Define 'minimal delay' as a specific time duration (e.g., < 30 seconds) to allow for proper operational planning.
The system shall process a sustained input data rate of 1.6 Gbytes/sec with a maximum end-to-end processing latency of less than X milliseconds per lag set.
The system shall provide sufficient buffer storage to handle a burst of 10 Gbytes of incoming data over a 500ms window without dropping packets.
The system shall provide a local buffer capable of storing at least 30 minutes of processed data to maintain operations during a temporary loss of the E2E system.

OPEN: The PRD lacks requirements for audit logging of administrative actions or security-relevant events beyond simple access attempts. - The system shall maintain an immutable audit log of all administrative actions, configuration changes, and security-related events, including timestamps and user identifiers.

OPEN: The PRD does not specify how the 'unique identification' is managed or if multi-factor authentication (MFA) is required for administrative access. - Administrative access to the system shall require multi-factor authentication.
OPEN: The PRD lacks requirements for session management, such as idle timeouts or maximum session duration. - The system shall automatically terminate user sessions after 15 minutes of inactivity.

OPEN: The PRD mentions that initial hardware specifications will be increased over time, but provides no roadmap or upper bound for the total cluster capacity. - Define the maximum expected scale of the cluster in terms of node count and aggregate throughput to ensure the architecture supports future expansion.

OPEN: The PRD mentions that initial deployment specifications will be 'increased over time' but provides no target growth metrics or upper bounds for the system's scalability. - The system architecture shall support a modular increase in processing nodes to handle a throughput increase of up to 500% over the initial 1.6 Gbytes/sec baseline without requiring a redesign of the core messaging middleware.
